searchText: Hello guys, does eip-4844 support range proof of blob data to KZG commitment? <@1152594466931228812> could you be a little more specific? i want to prove a subset of blob data belong to a specific address (that address posts blob data on chain), but i have so far found no inclusion proof of blob data. Gotcha thanks. I don't believe eip4844 directly supports this, though you may be able to do it yourself. For example, if you structure part of the blob data as a Merkle tree, you could generate your own inclusion proofs. But that doesn't feel like a great solution. <@592004585506340885> thanks bro, I did see some blogs that said it could be done with KZG commitment, but I couldn't find any technical documentation. It might be possible. Hopefully someone else can chime in. Good question though. So I was wrong. I forgot that you can generate proofs for individual elements in a blob with `compute_kzg_proof(blob, z) -> (proof, y)`. I think this is what you want. This blog does a great job of explaining it: https://pat.net/ckzg/ <@592004585506340885> really appreciated that bro. I just confused about what z or y stands for in the formula of KZG, I should learn more about zero knowledge. Here is a hackmd by lion on it: https://hackmd.io/@dapplion/blob_sharing#Appendix-KZG-commitment-proofs-for-data-subset <@427491045308235776> Thanks, even if the KZG commitment can be used to verify a field element in blob, but it costs 50000 gas (by using precompiled contract: 0x0a). I am not sure if 0x0a is compatible with proving multiple elements. You mentioned hackmd (https://hackmd.io/@dapplion/blob_sharing#Appendix-KZG-commitment-proofs-for-data-subset) said that using pairing check to prove a subset belong to a commitment, the pairing check (bls12381.PairingCheck ?) is still in the next upgrade plan and has not been activated on the mainnet. If you use 0x0a as is, then you would need to call it for every ~32 bytes of data that you want to prove is a subset of a particular blob. Yep; EIP2537 introduces the pairing check that is noted in that hackmd since the curve being used is bls12-381. I checked the EIP and it says the cost of a pairing is `43_000*k + 65_000` This is out of sync with 0x0a so I imagine that that will get updated

excerpts.content: <@1152594466931228812> could you be a little more specific?

excerpts.author: vinsmoke_42234
excerpts.content: i want to prove a subset of blob data belong to a specific address (that address posts blob data on chain), but i have so far found no inclusion  proof of blob data.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Gotcha thanks. I don't believe eip4844 directly supports this, though you may be able to do it yourself. For example, if you structure part of the blob data as a Merkle tree, you could generate your own inclusion proofs. But that doesn't feel like a great solution.

excerpts.author: vinsmoke_42234
excerpts.content: <@592004585506340885> thanks bro, I did see some blogs that said it could be done with KZG commitment, but I couldn't find any technical documentation.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: It might be possible. Hopefully someone else can chime in. Good question though.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: So I was wrong. I forgot that you can generate proofs for individual elements in a blob with `compute_kzg_proof(blob, z) -> (proof, y)`. I think this is what you want. This blog does a great job of explaining it: https://pat.net/ckzg/
